title: Number Recap (Y9 Foundation)
summary: A whiteboard recap before the Year 9 Number 1 assessment, in order of the marks each block carries: decimals, scaling and multiplying; estimating and money; prime factors and HCF; order of operations; negatives and squares. Question 1 of each block is cold and gives the tally for the next lesson's starter.

els.text:
•  Question 1: on your own, no help. Hold it up.
•  We sort out any mistakes together.
•  Questions 2 and 3: have another go.

slides.title: Decimals: add and subtract

items.title: Work out $6.84 + 3.57$
question: Work out $6.84 + 3.57$.
explanation: Line up the decimal points: $6.84$ above $3.57$.
Add from the right, carrying when a column reaches $10$.
items.rationale: Line up the decimal points, then add column by column.

items.title: Work out $8.2 - 3.45$
question: Work out $8.2 - 3.45$.
explanation: Fill the gap with a zero so both have the same number of decimal places: $8.20 - 3.45$.
Line up the decimal points and subtract: $8.20 - 3.45 = 4.75$
items.rationale: Placeholder zero, line up the points, subtract.

items.title: Find the difference between $9.06$ and $4.8$
question: Find the difference between $9.06$ and $4.8$.
explanation: Fill the gap with a zero so both have the same number of decimal places: $9.06 - 4.80$.
Line up the decimal points and subtract: $9.06 - 4.80 = 4.26$
items.rationale: Placeholder zero, line up the points, subtract.

slides.brief: Question 1 is cold: tally the boards. Lining up the points and the placeholder zero (8.2 as 8.20) are the usual slips. The third question is a spare.

slides.title: Multiply and divide by 10, 100, 1000

items.title: Work out $4.05 \times 100$
question: Work out $4.05 \times 100$.
explanation: Multiplying by $100$ moves every digit 2 places to the left.
items.rationale: The digits move; the decimal point does not.

items.title: Work out $7.3 \div 1,000$
question: Work out $7.3 \div 1,000$.
explanation: Dividing by $1,000$ moves every digit 3 places to the right.
items.rationale: The digits move; the decimal point does not.

items.title: Work out $0.63 \times 1,000$
question: Work out $0.63 \times 1,000$.
explanation: Multiplying by $1,000$ moves every digit 3 places to the left.
items.rationale: The digits move; the decimal point does not.

slides.brief: Question 1 is cold. Say 'the digits move' not 'the point moves'. The third question is a spare.

items.title: Work out $67 \times 43$
question: Work out $67 \times 43$.
items.rationale: Grid or partition: four small products, then add.

items.title: Work out $54 \times 28$
question: Work out $54 \times 28$.
items.rationale: Grid or partition: four small products, then add.

items.title: Work out $83 \times 36$
question: Work out $83 \times 36$.

slides.brief: Question 1 is cold. Students show the grid or the four products on the board, not just the answer (3 marks on the test). The third question is a spare.

slides.title: Which is closest to a fraction?

items.title: Which is closest to $\dfrac{1}{4}$?
question: Which is closest to $\dfrac{1}{4}$?
$0.22 \qquad \dfrac{3}{10} \qquad 0.27 \qquad \dfrac{6}{25}$
explanation: The smallest gap is $0.01$, so $\dfrac{6}{25}$ is closest.
items.rationale: Convert to decimals, then compare the distance from the target. The biggest or smallest is not the answer.

items.title: Which is closest to $\dfrac{1}{5}$?
question: Which is closest to $\dfrac{1}{5}$?
$0.18 \qquad \dfrac{3}{20} \qquad 0.23 \qquad \dfrac{4}{25}$
explanation: The smallest gap is $0.02$, so $0.18$ is closest.
items.rationale: Convert to decimals, then compare the distance from the target. The biggest or smallest is not the answer.

items.title: Which is closest to $\dfrac{3}{4}$?
question: Which is closest to $\dfrac{3}{4}$?
$0.72 \qquad \dfrac{4}{5} \qquad 0.78 \qquad \dfrac{37}{50}$
explanation: The smallest gap is $0.01$, so $\dfrac{37}{50}$ is closest.
items.rationale: Convert to decimals, then compare the distance from the target. The biggest or smallest is not the answer.

slides.brief: Question 1 is cold. The point is the distance from the target, not which is biggest. The third question is a spare.

items.title: Estimate: $\dfrac{28.7 \times 9.8}{0.52}$
question: Estimate: $\dfrac{28.7 \times 9.8}{0.52}$

items.title: Estimate: $\dfrac{6.1 \times 19.7}{0.39}$
question: Estimate: $\dfrac{6.1 \times 19.7}{0.39}$

slides.title: Money: which is the best buy?

items.title: Plan X: £5 a month plus 4p for each text. Plan Y: 6p for each text. Sam sends 150 texts. Which plan is cheaper?
question: Plan X: £5 a month plus 4p for each text. Plan Y: 6p for each text. Sam sends 150 texts. Which plan is cheaper?
explanation: £9 is less than £11, so Plan Y is cheaper.
items.rationale: Cost each plan for the same number of texts in the same unit, then compare.

items.title: A phone plan charges 4p a minute for the first 20 minutes and 6p a minute after that. How much is a 50-minute call?
question: A phone plan charges 4p a minute for the first 20 minutes and 6p a minute after that. How much is a 50-minute call?
items.rationale: A tiered price: cost each band separately, then add.

items.title: Taxi A charges £3 plus 80p a mile. Taxi B charges £1.50 a mile. Which is cheaper for 5 miles, and by how much?
question: Taxi A charges £3 plus 80p a mile. Taxi B charges £1.50 a mile. Which is cheaper for 5 miles, and by how much?
explanation: £7 is less than £7.50, so Taxi A is cheaper by £0.50.
items.rationale: Same method with mixed pounds and pence: change everything to pence first, or everything to pounds.

slides.brief: Question 1 is cold. Cost every option in the same unit, then compare in a sentence (the last mark on the test). The third question is a spare.

slides.title: Prime factors

items.title: Write $90$ as a product of its prime factors
question: Write $90$ as a product of its prime factors.
explanation: Split into a pair of factors: $90 = 9 \times 10$.
Keep splitting until every branch ends in a prime: $9 = 3 \times 3$, $\;10 = 2 \times 5$.
items.rationale: A factor tree, circle the primes, then write the product in order.

items.title: Write $140$ as a product of its prime factors
question: Write $140$ as a product of its prime factors.
explanation: Split into a pair of factors: $140 = 14 \times 10$.
Keep splitting until every branch ends in a prime: $14 = 2 \times 7$, $\;10 = 2 \times 5$.
items.rationale: A factor tree, circle the primes, then write the product in order.

items.title: Write $252$ as a product of its prime factors
question: Write $252$ as a product of its prime factors.
explanation: Split into a pair of factors: $252 = 4 \times 63$.
Keep splitting until every branch ends in a prime: $4 = 2 \times 2$, $\;63 = 3 \times 3 \times 7$.
items.rationale: A factor tree, circle the primes, then write the product in order.

slides.brief: Question 1 is cold. Students draw the tree on their boards. The third question is a spare.

slides.title: HCF from prime factors

items.title: $126 = 2 \times 3^{2} \times 7$ and $84 = 2^{2} \times 3 \times 7$
question: $126 = 2 \times 3^{2} \times 7$ and $84 = 2^{2} \times 3 \times 7$.
Find the HCF of $126$ and $84$.
explanation: Circle the primes that are in both: $2, 3, 7$.
items.rationale: Both numbers' primes are shown: take every prime they share, at the lower power, and multiply.

items.title: $150 = 2 \times 3 \times 5^{2}$
question: $150 = 2 \times 3 \times 5^{2}$.
Write $210$ as a product of primes, then find the HCF of $150$ and $210$.
explanation: $2 \times 3 \times 5 = 30$, so the HCF of $150$ and $210$ is $30$.
items.rationale: As the test asks: write one number in primes yourself, use the other as given, then take the shared primes.

items.title: Find the HCF of $132$ and $198$
question: Find the HCF of $132$ and $198$.
items.rationale: Prime factors of both, then the shared primes.

slides.brief: Question 1 is cold: both prime forms are given. Question 2 has one given, as on the test. The third question is a spare.

slides.title: Order of operations

items.title: Work out $2 + 3 \times 4 - 1$
question: Work out $2 + 3 \times 4 - 1$.
explanation: Add and subtract from left to right: $13$
items.rationale: Multiplication before addition and subtraction.

items.title: Add one pair of brackets so that
question: Add one pair of brackets so that
$2 + 3 \times 4 - 1 = 19$
items.rationale: Brackets change the order; try the placements and check.

items.title: Dev works out $6 \times (10 - 4)$
question: Dev works out $6 \times (10 - 4)$.
His working: $6 \times (10 - 4) = 60 - 4 = 56$
What mistake has he made?
answer: He multiplied by $10$ and ignored the bracket: it is $36$
explanation: He did $6 \times 10$ first, but the bracket must be worked out first.
items.rationale: Brackets come first, even when the multiplication is written before them.

slides.brief: Question 1 is cold. Question 3 is the error-spot; the sentence 'he did ... but should have done ...' is the answer. The third question is a spare.

slides.title: Negatives and squares

items.title: Write in order, smallest first:
question: Write in order, smallest first:
$-9, \quad 4, \quad -2, \quad -15, \quad 0$
explanation: The negatives are smallest, and the bigger the number after the minus sign, the smaller the number: $-15 < -9 < -2$.
items.rationale: Order on a number line, negatives first.

items.title: Work out $(-6)^2$
question: Work out $(-6)^2$.
Then work out $-6^2$.
explanation: $(-6)^2 = -6 \times -6 = 36$, since a negative times a negative is positive.
$-6^2$: square the $6$ first, then make it negative: $-(6 \times 6) = -36$.
items.rationale: The brackets decide what is squared.

items.title: Zoe says $(-5)^2 = -25$
question: Zoe says $(-5)^2 = -25$.
What mistake has she made?
answer: She squared only the $5$ and kept the minus: $(-5)^2 = 25$
explanation: She worked out $5 \times 5 = 25$ and put the minus back on.
$(-5)^2$ means $-5 \times -5$, and a negative times a negative is positive: $25$.
items.rationale: Squaring a negative gives a positive.

slides.brief: Question 1 is cold. Squaring a negative is the idea to leave them with (the test asks whether a squared negative can be negative). The third question is a spare.
